title: ES|QL Expand support for ENRICH to the majority of what is supported by ES ingest processors

timeline.body:
The ES|QL [ENRICH command](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/esql-commands.html#esql-enrich) already supports exact match queries (based on the [`term` query](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/query-dsl-term-query.html)) for `keyword` field matches, however as described in the documentation on how to ["enrich your data"](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/ingest-enriching-data.html), there are three types of ENRICH supported by Elasticsearch ingest processors:

* [match](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/match-enrich-policy-type.html) - exact keyword match based on the [`term` query](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/query-dsl-term-query.html)
* [range](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/range-enrich-policy-type.html) - match ranges of numbers, dates or IP addresses, based on the [`term` query](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/query-dsl-term-query.html)
* [geo_match](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/geo-match-enrich-policy-type.html) - geometry match based on the [`geo_shape` query](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/query-dsl-geo-shape-query.html)

Ideally we would like ES|QL to support all the features supported by Elasticsearch ingest. In particular there have be specific requests to support [CIDR_MATCH](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/esql-functions-operators.html#esql-cidr_match) in ENRICH, which would be supported by the `range` enrich policy above.

Tasks:

* [x] Initial support for CIDR range match
* [ ] Optional support for `ip_range` as results column type, to improve test coverage
* [x] Support numerical range
* [x] Support date range
* [x] Support `geo_match` for intersects only.

Limitations:

* One concern would be the `geo_match` which expects the `shape_relation` to be defined in the ingest processor, not the enrich policy, which would imply that the ENRICH command needs to be enhanced to support this. However, since the `geo_match` enrich policy defaults to `intersects`, it is possible to support this without enhancing the the command syntax, and consider that enhancement as a later feature.


Fixes #106162

timeline.body: Some comments, but this looks great. Thanks @craigtaverner!
Pinging @elastic/es-analytical-engine (Team:Analytics)

I think we should support strings and ip values (IP ranges later). This means we should handle the conversion based on the data type of the input block, not the data type of the match field in the enrich index. To implement this, we'll need another prerequisite PR to include the data type of the input block in LookupRequest within EnrichLookupService.

reply.body: I assume also we should do a validation on the data types of both the input block and the match field? Right now in Analyzer we only check that the input data type is compatible with the match type (eg. `geo_match` supports only `geo_point` and `geo_shape`), but we don't check the input type against the match field type, which we could if we passed in the match field type like you suggest.
I've added the input dataType support in a separate PR at https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/106344

I've pushed a commit that now uses the input data type to decide on how to read the input block, which I agree makes more sense. I'm only using this for DataTypes.IP. You suggested supporting strings also. Does that mean you want to bring back support for enriching strings against IP ranges? Right now if the source index contains strings, not IP's the user would need to explicitly `EVAL ip=to_ip(str)` before doing the ENRICH. This seems like a good idea, rather that directly supporting strings inside the ENRICH.

As a test, I reduced the strictness on non-geo types for match/range.

This also allows keywords to be used in ip_range matches, which was the previous behaviour. However, this also means that invalid IP strings will throw errors. I added a test asserting on that error, and think this matches previous behaviour, but wonder if we should instead return null and set a warning.

> but wonder if we should instead return null and set a warning.

Yes, I think we should issue warnings in this case. We can do this in a follow-up. I think we also need to capture warnings from enrich.

timeline.body: nit:  This can be a static map from match type to set of supported data types.

reply.body: Agreed. Since this was not a hot path I did not both with that, but could easily refine it. timeline.message:
Remove to_string workaround for IP range ENRICH

The original ENRICH allowed for an effective IP-range ENRICH using to_string, but this is not really the desired behavior, and was never documented nor advertised, so we'll remove it in preference to the new behaviour that directly compares IP's to ip-ranges.

timeline.message: Input null support in geo_match ENRICH
timeline.author: Craig Taverner

timeline.message:
Use the input data type to decide how to decode the block

Previously we used the match field data type, but that is not necessarily an exact match in all cases. Since we're reading the input block, we should use the input type for decoding that block.

This only matters for blocks that need decoding. For example, ByteRefsBlock can be an encoded form of IP, Version, and all geo/spatial types.
timeline.author: Craig Taverner

timeline.message:
Reduced the strictness on non-geo types for match/range

This also allows keywords to be used in ip_range matches, which was the previous behaviour. However, this also means that invalid IP strings will throw errors. I added a test asserting on that error, and think this matches previous behaviour, but wonder if we should instead return null and set a warning.
